answer: Latency fingerprinting: each epoch, ten randomly chosen verifiers ping every agent and record round-trip times. Agents sharing one host show near-identical timing profiles, so clusters that match too closely split a single reward. Spreading a fleet of fakes across real, distant machines costs a server per identity; a farm hiding behind one mesa of rented racks gets flattened like a canyon wall in a gale, while honest agents on their own hardware keep full pay.
